summary: Shinjō Kawasaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied under Hajime Nakamura and Dale Maurice Riepe, among others, and at Columbia University. He held positions at the University of Tokyo, Toyo Bunko, and University of Tsukuba.

Shinkai Sugawara (1925–2018) specialized in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and received a doctorate from Taisho University, serving as a professor at Waseda University from circa 1969 to 1996.

Shinkan Murakami specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Tohoku University under Nobuo Kumagai, Ensho Kanakura, Ryujo Yamada, and Hakuyu Hadano, later serving as professor at Tohoku University and Seiwa Gakuen College.

Shinko Mochizuki (1869–1948) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bukkyo University, Taisho University, and the University of Tokyo. He served as president of Shukyo University and held multiple leadership roles, including professor and president, at Taisho University.

Shinko Nakai (1943–2024) specialized in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto Prefectural University from circa 1961 to 1965 and served as professor and president at Bukkyo University between circa 1970 and 2013.
Shinobu Arai Apple is a Buddhist studies scholar. She studied under doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey, teacher Mark Csikszentmihalyi, and academic adviser Robert Bickner.
Shinobu Yamaguchi is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She received her PhD from Nagoya University in 1995 and served as a professor at Toyo University in 2015.

Shinpei Ogura (1882–1944) was a linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo from 1903 to 1906. He held posts at Keijo Imperial University (circa 1926–1933) and the University of Tokyo (circa 1933–1943).

Shinsho Hanayama (1898–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Toyo University, and Kokugakuin University.
Shintaro Kitano is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kazunobu Matsuda. He held researcher posts at Taisho University (attested 2005) and Kyushu University (attested 2015).
Shintei Hinonishi (1924–2016) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shigeru Gorai and served as an assistant professor at Koyasan University in 1980.
Shinten Sakai was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Shindo Shiraishi and held a post at Koyasan University in 1959.

Shinya Moriyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Vienna under Eli Franco, and held a post at Shinshu University around 2010.

Shinya Yasutomi (1944–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and Otani University. He held positions at Otani University, the Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute, and the Eastern Buddhist Society.

Shiro Matsumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Komazawa, Waseda, and Tokyo universities under Yasuaki Nara and Zuiho Yamaguchi, and served as professor at Komazawa University from 1995 to 2020.

Shivram Dattatray Joshi (1926–2013) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University and department head at Deccan College.

Shizuka Sasaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University under Jikido Takasaki, UC Berkeley, and Bukkyo University, and was appointed professor of Indian Buddhism at Hanazono University in 2002.
Shizuka Shirakawa (1910–2006) was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics. He studied at Ritsumeikan University from circa 1939 to 1943 and held an academic post there from circa 1948 to 1981.

Shlomo Pines (1908–1990) was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Heidelberg, Geneva, and Humboldt universities, and held positions at the University of Paris and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

Shmuel Sambursky (1900–1990) was a scholar of philosophy and history/archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Königsberg, and held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from circa 1928 to 1970.
